text:
sara-cust: Hi, since ~03:10 UTC our agents in us-west2 can't establish mTLS to the private control plane. Connections fail immediately during TLS handshake. Our inline proxy logs: 'tlsv1 alert internal error' and 'received close_notify'. Control plane host: cp-us-west.redwood-private.example.com

maria: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact proxy error lines and the source IP (or NAT IP) you're using? Any recent NAT/proxy changes?

sara-cust: Proxy excerpts: 'SSL_read: error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher' and 'TLS record length 5 mismatch'. Source (post-NAT) IP: 198.51.100.42. We rotated our NAT gateway this morning and pushed a new inline inspection policy.

ryan_netops: Thanks. That smells like ClientHello being split across TCP segments and the inspection device not handling reassembly. Can you capture a pcap from your egress NAT box to the control plane IP and share? Example:
```
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/cp.pcap -s 0 host cp-us-west.redwood-private.example.com and port 443
```
And run an openssl test:
```
openssl s_client -connect cp-us-west.redwood-private.example.com:443 -servername cp-us-west.redwood-private.example.com -msg
```

sara-cust: Uploaded pcap: https://cust-files.example.com/cp-us-west-cp.pcap. Our appliance is an inline SSL-inspection box (vendor: Palo Alto).

jasper_engineer: I had a near-identical case where PA did inline TLS inspect and flagged the TLS record as malformed when ClientHello was split. Can you paste the first few packets in hex or a Wireshark export?

sara-cust: From tcpdump -nn -r cp-us-west-cp.pcap:
```
# packet 1: TCP seg with TLS record header only (5 bytes)
# packet 2: following segment contains the rest of the ClientHello
```
Wireshark labels: 'Malformed TLS record' and 'Client Hello, Handshake Protocol: Client Hello' spanning two TCP segments.

maria: That confirms fragmentation. Inline inspectors that don't reassemble TCP streams before TLS parsing will drop the handshake. Two quick mitigations to validate:
1) Bypass the inline inspection for the control-plane FQDN/IP (egress allowlist)
2) Apply an MSS clamp on your NAT/gateway (e.g., 1400) to avoid segmentation of the ClientHello.

sara-cust: I temporarily bypassed the inspection (policy change) and retried. With proxy bypass, openssl s_client shows:
```
SSL-Session:
    Verify return code: 0 (ok)
```
Connections succeed when bypassed.

jasper_engineer: Long-term fixes: ask the vendor to enable TCP stream reassembly for SSL inspection, or whitelist mTLS endpoints so inspection is not performed. Also verify the inspection device isn't stripping intermediary certs/chains — that can also break client verification. We'll open an internal escalation to collect control-plane-side logs during your failure window.

edge-probe-bot: probe: us-west heartbeat from 203.0.113.45 -> cp-us-west at 3123456830: OK

ryan_netops: If vendor changes are slow, keep using a dedicated egress NAT IP that bypasses inspection or keep MSS clamp. For Palo Alto the specific setting is 'TCP reassembly' (or 'Stream Reassembly' on older PAN-OS).

sara-cust: We'll request vendor change and apply MSS clamp to 1400 for now. Can Redwood share canonical egress allowlist and ports to whitelist?

maria: Docs link: https://docs.redwood.com/private/networking#egress . Key ports: 443 (control plane API TLS). I'll DM you the exact control-plane IP ranges for your region and open the escalation ticket attaching your pcap + proxy logs. Thanks — looks like a customer-side inline inspection + segmentation issue, resolved by bypass or MSS clamp for now.
